q.t: Find the compound interest on ₹1000 at 10% per year for 2 years, compounded yearly (in ₹).
q.e: Year 1: 10% of 1000 = 100 → 1100. Year 2: 10% of 1100 = 110 → 1210. Interest = 210. The second year earns interest on the first year’s interest too.

q.t: Find the amount on ₹1000 at 10% per year for 2 years, compounded yearly (in ₹).
q.e: Each year multiplies the money by 1.1: 1000 × 1.1 × 1.1 = 1210.

q.t: Which is the formula for the amount at compound interest (compounded yearly for n years)?
q.e: Each year the money is multiplied by (1 + R/100). After n years that multiplication has happened n times.

q.t: For the FIRST year, compound interest (compounded yearly) and simple interest on the same sum are:
q.e: In year one there is no earlier interest to earn interest on, so both are just R% of the principal.

q.t: Find the interest on ₹5000 at 10% per year for 1 year (in ₹).
Compound interest equals:
q.e: The interest is whatever the money has grown by.

q.t: When interest is compounded half-yearly, we use:
o: Half the rate and twice the number of periods
Twice the rate and half the periods
Half the rate and half the periods
q.e: Interest is added every 6 months: each addition is at half the yearly rate, and there are two additions per year.

q.t: Find the amount on ₹2000 at 5% per year for 2 years, compounded yearly (in ₹).
Interest that is earned on earlier interest as well as on the principal is called:
q.e: The interest is ‘compounded’ — added to the principal so that it earns interest too.

q.t: ₹100 is invested at 10% per year compounded yearly. Find the amount after 2 years (in ₹).
Find the compound interest on ₹8000 at 5% per year for 2 years (in ₹).
Find the amount on ₹10,000 at 10% per year for 3 years, compounded yearly (in ₹).
Find the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹5000 at 10% per year for 2 years (in ₹).
q.e: CI = 1050 and SI = 1000. The extra ₹50 is the interest on the first year’s ₹500 of interest.

q.t: Find the compound interest on ₹4000 for 1 year at 10% per year, compounded half-yearly (in ₹).
A town of 20,000 people grows by 5% each year. Find the population after 2 years.
A machine worth ₹50,000 loses 10% of its value every year. Find its value after 2 years (in ₹).
q.e: Each year it keeps 90%: 50,000 → 45,000 → 40,500. Depreciation multiplies by (1 − R/100).

q.t: Find the compound interest on ₹6250 at 8% per year for 2 years (in ₹).
Find the amount on ₹12,000 at 15% per year for 2 years, compounded yearly (in ₹).
What sum amounts to ₹1210 in 2 years at 10% per year compound interest (in ₹)?
Find the compound interest on ₹16,000 for 1 year at 5% per year, compounded half-yearly (in ₹).
₹5000 becomes ₹6050 in 2 years at compound interest. Find the rate percent per year.
In how many years will ₹8000 amount to ₹9261 at 5% per year compound interest?
The difference between the compound and simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 4% per year is ₹32. Find the sum (in ₹).
q.e: For 2 years the difference is P × (R/100)² = P × 0.0016 = 32, so P = 20,000.

q.t: ₹10,000 is invested for 2 years at 10% for the first year and 20% for the second. Find the amount (in ₹).
Find the compound interest on ₹8000 for 1 1/2 years at 10% per year, compounded half-yearly (in ₹).
A town’s population is 9261 after growing by 5% a year for 3 years. What was it 3 years ago?
A machine loses 20% of its value each year and is worth ₹64,000 after 2 years. Find its original value (in ₹).
Find the compound interest on ₹15,625 at 4% per year for 3 years (in ₹).
A sum amounts to ₹4840 in 2 years and to ₹5324 in 3 years at compound interest. Find the rate percent per year.
q.e: The third year’s interest is 5324 − 4840 = 484, earned on 4840: 484/4840 = 10%.

q.t: Bacteria in a culture increase by 10% every hour. There are 20,000 now. How many will there be after 2 hours?
The difference between the compound and simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 10% per year is ₹93. Find the sum (in ₹).
q.e: CI = 0.331P and SI = 0.3P, so the difference is 0.031P = 93 and P = 3000.

q.t: A sum amounts to ₹2420 in 2 years and ₹2662 in 3 years at compound interest. Find the sum (in ₹).
At what rate percent per year does a sum become 27/8 times itself in 3 years at compound interest?
Find the compound interest on ₹16,000 for 9 months at 20% per year, compounded quarterly (in ₹).
q.e: Quarterly rate = 5%, and 9 months = 3 quarters: 16,000 × (21/20)³ = 18,522. Interest = 2522.

q.t: A town of 10,000 grows by 10% in year one, shrinks by 10% in year two and grows by 10% in year three. Find the final population.
A sum doubles in 5 years at compound interest. In how many years does it become 8 times itself?
q.e: 8 = 2 × 2 × 2 — three doublings, each taking 5 years. (With simple interest it would take 35 years.)

q.t: The simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 5% per year is ₹400. Find the compound interest for the same time and rate (in ₹).
Find the compound interest on ₹6000 for 2 1/2 years at 10% per year, compounded yearly (in ₹).
q.e: Two full years: 6000 × 1.21 = 7260. The half year adds 5%: 7260 × 1.05 = 7623. Interest = 1623.

q.t: A man borrows ₹20,000 at 10% per year compound interest and repays ₹12,000 at the end of the first year. How much must he pay at the end of the second year to clear the loan (in ₹)?
q.e: After year 1 he owes 22,000; he pays 12,000, leaving 10,000. That grows by 10% to 11,000.

q.t: A scooter’s value falls from ₹25,000 to ₹20,250 in 2 years. Find the yearly rate of depreciation (in %).
